claims.text: High-entropy alloys subjected to high-pressure, high-temperature treatment can exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition within a narrow temperature window.
High-pressure, high-temperature treatment can improve the strength of high-entropy alloys relative to conventional alloys.
High-pressure, high-temperature treatment can improve the ductility of high-entropy alloys relative to conventional alloys.
The proposed intervention is high-pressure, high-temperature treatment of a high-entropy alloy.
High-pressure, high-temperature treatment influences grain size in the high-entropy alloy.
High-pressure, high-temperature treatment influences phase distribution in the high-entropy alloy.
Treatment-induced microstructural changes lead to improved strength and ductility.
High-pressure, high-temperature treatment may reduce the effects of temper embrittlement in high-entropy alloys.
Conventional alloys exhibit temper embrittlement and lose ductility within a narrow temperature window.
The effectiveness of the treatment depends on temperature and pressure conditions.
